clue.text: Monastic hour's brought back inaudible prayer

indicators.note: something brought back returns the way it came, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: terce is the monastic office said at the third hour; the plural with S

explanation.surface: A monk's devotions at a set hour are recited under the breath.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Mass, the secret is a prayer the priest says silently over the offerings, so it is a liturgical term for a prayer not heard.

clue.text: Get worked up or withdraw when losing heart

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle of the word goes, taking the central letters away

parts.note: to subtract is to take away or withdraw

explanation.surface: A choice between getting agitated and pulling out when discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get worked up' is not emotional here: to subact is to work up, reduce or subdue something.
explanation.definitionFit: Subact is an old verb meaning to work up or bring under, a rare dictionary sense of reducing by working.

clue.text: A prominent feature in cold country brings a lot of laughter

indicators.note: in places one group of letters inside the other pair

parts.note: a jutting chin is a prominent facial feature
taken as written
C for cold, as on a tap
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A striking landmark in a frozen land makes everyone laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachinnation is loud, immoderate laughter, a lot of it.

clue.text: Only half of story-tellers used a communications device

indicators.note: keeping only half means the back half of the word is dropped

parts.note: raconteurs tell stories

explanation.surface: Some of the yarn-spinners talked over a radio set.
explanation.definitionFit: A racon is a radar beacon, a navigation device that answers a ship's radar with an identifying signal.

clue.text: Underweight? Hope somehow lies within this chemical compound

indicators.note: what lies within something is enclosed by it

parts.note: underweight means thin

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are got into shape in some unstated way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dieter wonders whether optimism is the secret of some chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Thiophen (thiophene) is a sulphur-containing ring compound found in coal tar, a chemical compound.

clue.text: Harry once being funny person celebrating

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Sir Harry ..., the Scottish music-hall comedian of the early twentieth century
second meaning: one who lauds, praising someone

explanation.surface: An old-time entertainer called Harry was a comic at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A lauder is literally one who lauds or praises, and Harry Lauder was a famous Scottish stage comic.

clue.text: Psychiatrist harsh once, European fellow to be ignored

parts.note: asper is an obsolete word for harsh or rough

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so those letters go

parts.note: a German is a European
a fellow is a man; these letters are dropped

explanation.surface: A once-stern psychiatrist dismisses a colleague from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Asperger was the Austrian child psychiatrist who described the syndrome named after him.

clue.text: Lost during war when in country boat

indicators.note: in places one set of letters inside the other

parts.note: the United Kingdom
MIA is military shorthand for missing in action

explanation.surface: A vessel goes missing in a wartime country.
explanation.definitionFit: An umiak is an open Inuit boat of skins on a wooden frame.

clue.text: Old dear ageing, somehow avoiding a sudden decline

indicators.note: somehow says the letters fall into place in some unstated order
avoiding something means doing without it, so that letter is left out

parts.note: taken as written
one A is the letter removed

explanation.surface: An elderly lady grows older and somehow escapes a sharp fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Dégringolade is French-derived for a rapid fall or collapse, a sudden decline in fortune.

clue.text: You headed up round tip of the island

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: ye is the old form of you
O is round in shape

indicators.note: the tip is the very first point, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: Someone sails up and round the point of a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot (ait) is a small island, especially in a river like the Thames.

clue.text: Cow in Yorkshire location yielding meat

indicators.note: yielding means giving up, so those letters are surrendered from the place name

parts.note: Rotherham is a town in South Yorkshire
ham is cured pork; these letters go

explanation.surface: Cattle in a Yorkshire town are being raised for meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rother is an old dialect word for an ox or cow, as in rother-beast.

clue.text: Sheepish noise by this maiden offering Arab ideology

parts.note: the bleat of a sheep
taken as written
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A timid girl bleats out a political creed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places one piece next to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Baathism is the doctrine of the Baath party, a pan-Arab socialist movement in Syria and Iraq.

clue.text: Risky game when rat's destroyed berry

indicators.note: read with 'destroyed', the clue says the game is left once the named creature has been wiped out of it

parts.note: the casino card game
the rodent is the part taken away

explanation.surface: A gambling game goes wrong when a rodent wrecks a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacca is the botanical Latin term for a berry, used in Chambers as an English word.

clue.text: Vocal phenomenon of a baa, say, outside university

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: lying outside means wrapping round, so one part encloses the other

parts.note: blat is to bleat, and a baa is an example
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A linguist notices something odd in a sheep's bleat round the campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablaut is vowel gradation, the change of vowel in sing, sang, sung, a phenomenon of vowels in language.

clue.text: Glutton hugged by drunkard? This could stop booze flowing

indicators.note: being hugged means being held inside someone's arms, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drinker
a greedy eater

explanation.surface: A greedy eater is embraced by a drunk, prompting thoughts of stopping the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a peg or tap that plugs the vent of a cask, controlling the flow of liquor.

clue.text: Hate sound of a tedious person with additional aspiration

indicators.note: something additional is added in, here slipped into the middle of the spoken phrase
the sound of a phrase is how it is spoken, so we want letters that say the phrase

parts.note: a bore is a tedious person; said with a non-rhotic accent
aspiration is the breathed H sound

explanation.surface: Someone loathes the voice of a dull person who also breathes heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: In southern British speech the answer sounds just like 'a bore', apart from the breathed H in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor is to detest or loathe, a stronger synonym of hate.

clue.text: Where we all live? Absolutely!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: on the planet, our home

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the emphatic one in 'what on earth', which strengthens a question or a negative like 'at all'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase gives our planetary location, and as an intensifier it works like 'absolutely' or 'at all'.

clue.text: Awfully sweet and nice? Not college maids

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters come out jumbled
not means without, so that letter is left out of the mix

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for college; it is removed

explanation.surface: Some girls are terribly charming, but not the ones at university.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeny was a between-maid, a servant helping both cook and housemaid in a large household.

clue.text: Fliers have the ability to go above the stars!

indicators.note: in a down clue going above means coming first, so one piece precedes the other

parts.note: can means are able
Aries is a constellation and star sign

explanation.surface: Pilots are capable of soaring above the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaries are small songbirds, so they are creatures that fly.

clue.text: Old resident left on mountain

parts.note: L for left
the Eiger is a Swiss Alpine peak

explanation.surface: An elderly local has been left alone on the mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old resident' is not a pensioner: in old usage a leiger was a resident ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: Leiger (ledger) is an obsolete word for a resident, especially an ambassador stationed abroad.

clue.text: What animal painlessly changes into a monster?

indicators.note: changing into something means taking on a new form, so the letters are rearranged
without pain: the French word for pain, mal, is taken out of the word before

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, before the pain is removed

explanation.surface: A riddle about which creature can turn into a monster without hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: MAL is French for pain, so dropping it from ANIMAL leaves ANI.
explanation.definitionFit: In Maori legend a taniwha is a water monster or dragon lurking in rivers and the sea.

clue.text: You're no good, in retrospect, but not entirely a hopeless case

indicators.note: looking in retrospect means looking backwards, so the letters run right to left
only part of the run of words is used, so the answer is tucked inside them

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on someone, softened on reflection to 'not entirely hopeless'.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone or something beyond saving, a person doomed or a lost cause.

clue.text: Greek character stuck in mine, rolling around in muck

indicators.note: rolling around turns the whole thing over, so it is read backwards
something stuck in a thing is lodged inside it

parts.note: egg is old military slang for a mine or bomb
nu is the Greek letter N

explanation.surface: A Greek is trapped in a mine shaft, wallowing in filth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' is not the possessive: an egg is service slang for a bomb or mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunge is British slang for any sticky, messy substance, close in sense to muck or gunk.

clue.text: Flowering plant — plucking it's bad — awful stink emerges

indicators.note: bad signals the letters are in a poor order and need rearranging
what emerges comes out, so these letters are taken out of the mixture

parts.note: taken as written
the letters of stink, in any order, are removed

explanation.surface: Picking a flower is wrong, and a dreadful smell results.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilcup is a dialect name for the buttercup, a common yellow-flowering plant.

clue.text: Biological unit has new green identity

indicators.note: something new has been made afresh, so the following letters take a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
ID is the usual abbreviation for identity

explanation.surface: Something in biology is given a fresh environmentalist image.
explanation.definitionFit: In cell biology an energid is a nucleus together with the cytoplasm it controls, treated as a functional unit.

clue.text: Three journalists (one is upset) being transferred in America

definitions.note: a past participle in the passive sense

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so one copy reads backwards

parts.note: ED for editor, three times

explanation.surface: Three reporters are moved to the American office, one of them unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: In US usage to deed is to transfer property by deed, so deeded means conveyed.

clue.text: Jewish period that is ritualistic to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so just part of the run of words is taken

parts.note: spanning the end of the first word, the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A Jewish season is somewhat ceremonial in character.
explanation.definitionFit: Tisri (Tishri) is the first month of the Jewish civil year, a period of the calendar.

clue.text: Ancient city's in Mafia territory? Not so

indicators.note: not means without, so the following word's letters are dropped

parts.note: the Mafia's home island is Sicily
sic is Latin for so or thus

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an ancient city lay in Mafia country, and is told no.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilian means of Ilium, the ancient city of Troy, so it is the adjective for that city.

clue.text: Classical scholar establishing camp outside home after time

indicators.note: one thing lying outside another wraps round it

parts.note: laer is a variant of laager, a South African defensive camp of wagons

indicators.note: after places one piece to follow the other in the run of letters

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
in means at home

explanation.surface: An academic of the classics sets up a camp outside his home after a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latiner is one who knows Latin, a scholar of the classical language.

clue.text: Buffaloes are in short supply over North America

definitions.note: plural here; the word is used as a collective

indicators.note: in short supply means cut short, so the last letter is lost
in a down clue over means placed above, so one piece comes first

parts.note: taken as written
NA is the abbreviation for North America

explanation.surface: Bison have become scarce across North America.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests American bison, but the answer is an Asian animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The arna is the wild water buffalo of India.

clue.text: Everyone needing extra energy for walk

indicators.note: the first word needs the following ones joined on to complete it

parts.note: everyone means all
E for energy, with an extra E besides

explanation.surface: Everybody needs more pep before going for a stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: An allée is a formal avenue or tree-lined path in a garden, the kind of place one walks.

clue.text: Conservative facing endless peril is in desperately tricky situation

indicators.note: something endless has lost its final part, so the last letter is cut
facing puts one piece directly in front of the next

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a risk is a danger
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tory under constant danger is in a desperate fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of acute danger or difficulty, a desperately tricky situation.

clue.text: Grey piece of lead tossed back

indicators.note: tossed back means thrown back the way it came, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a drail is a weighted fish-hook, a piece of lead used in trolling

explanation.surface: Someone flings back a dull grey lump of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Liard is an old word for grey or dapple-grey, used of horses.

clue.text: Soldiers fuss about officer turning traitor

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so this word runs backwards

parts.note: GEN is the abbreviation for general
ado is a fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: Troops making a fuss about a commander who has gone over to the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' looks like the reversal signal, but it only joins wordplay to definition: X turning Y means X becomes Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Renegado is an older form of renegade, someone who deserts a cause or faith, a traitor.

clue.text: Lesser god has society gripped by fear

indicators.note: something gripped is held tight inside another's grasp

parts.note: panic is sudden fear
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A minor deity's followers are seized with terror.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitting, since panic is named after the god Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A panisc is a minor woodland deity, one of the attendants of Pan, so a lesser god.

clue.text: Legislative assembly needs to be reformed by Democrat

indicators.note: something reformed is reshaped into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A parliament must be overhauled by a Democratic member.
explanation.definitionFit: The Senedd is the Welsh Parliament in Cardiff, the devolved legislature of Wales.
